name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage "Perth" (guide status; listed first under Cities on Wikivoyage "Western Australia")
name_evidence.wording: "Perth — The state capital of Western Australia and one of the most remote large cities in the world"; districts City of Perth, Northbridge, Fremantle, The Coast, Swan Valley, The Suburbs

destinations.name: Rottnest Island
destinations.coordinates_source: OSM place=island relation 8145344 "Rottnest Island" (Photon); visual centre of the island (Thomson Bay settlement, the ferry landing, is 2.6 km east)

name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage "Rottnest Island" (own article, listed under "Perth surrounds" on Wikivoyage Perth); Tourism WA Rottnest Island page
name_evidence.wording: "Rottnest Island — Where locals like to relax and home to the irresistible quokkas"; Wikivoyage Perth: "One of the best day trips in Perth is to visit Rottnest Island"

destinations.name: Perth Hills
destinations.coordinates_source: centre of the bounding box of its pinned spots (no single visitor hub covers the scarp from Walyunga to Serpentine. Research may re-centre on Kalamunda or Mundaring visitor centre and widen the span.)

name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage "Perth/The Hills" (listed under "Outside the city" on Wikivoyage Perth); Experience Perth Hills / Destination Perth "Perth Hills" pages (cited in the verdicts)
name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage: "The Hills — Wine, trees, hills, parks, and dams" and "The Perth Hills is the 'brand' used by tourism bodies"

name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage "Western Australia" Cities list and Wikivoyage "Mandurah" (own article)
name_evidence.wording: "Mandurah — a rapidly growing city nestled between estuary and ocean is popular for fishing and crabbing"

destinations.name: Avon Valley
destinations.coordinates_source: centre of the bounding box of its pinned spots (no single hub: York, Northam and Toodyay are 22-48 km apart)

name_evidence.source: Destination Perth "Avon Valley" page and Avon Valley road trip (cited in the verdicts for Beverley, York Motor Museum, Mount Brown Lookout, Newcastle Gaol Museum); Wikivoyage Perth
name_evidence.wording: Wikivoyage Perth: "the famous wild flowers around Kings Park and the neighbouring Avon Valley region are blooming"; Destination Perth gives Beverley "its own section" of its Avon Valley page

spots.name: Kings Park and Botanic Garden
spots.bio: Inner-city bushland and botanic garden on Mount Eliza above the Swan River, with walks and views over the city.
spots.note: Perth's headline attraction, 3.6 km from the city centre.

spots.name: Fremantle Prison
spots.bio: UNESCO World Heritage convict-built prison in Fremantle, open for tours and exhibitions.
spots.note: Fremantle is filed under Perth (COVERAGE); 18 km from the city centre, inside the span.

spots.name: Fremantle
spots.bio: Historic port city whose heritage-listed West End is Australia's largest intact Victorian-era port streetscape.
spots.note: A town that is itself a draw (the West End streets and the Cappuccino Strip, which no other spot covers), so it is a spot beside its attractions; filed under Perth, not its own destination (COVERAGE names Fremantle → Perth). Fremantle West End is merged into it.

spots.name: Cottesloe Beach
spots.bio: Ocean beach west of central Perth with a heritage pavilion, swimming and sunsets over the Indian Ocean.
spots.note: Perth's best-known beach, 11 km from the centre.

spots.name: WA Museum Boola Bardip
spots.bio: The state museum in Perth's Cultural Centre, with eight permanent galleries of the state's natural and social history.
spots.note: The state museum, 0.8 km from the centre.

spots.name: Art Gallery of Western Australia
spots.bio: The state art gallery in Perth's Cultural Centre, showing contemporary, international and Indigenous art.
spots.note: Central Perth.

spots.name: Perth Mint
spots.bio: Australia's oldest operating mint, a gold refinery in central Perth with tours and gold-pour demonstrations.
spots.note: Central Perth.

spots.name: Swan Valley
spots.bio: Perth's nearest wine region, a valley of cellar doors, breweries and food producers on the city's north-eastern edge.
spots.note: A Wikivoyage district of Perth visited as a day trip from the city (about 20 km out); a wine region with no single winery kept, so the region itself is the spot.

spots.name: Elizabeth Quay
spots.bio: Riverside precinct on the Swan River in central Perth, with a footbridge, an island playground and a ferry jetty.
spots.note: Central Perth.

spots.name: Perth Zoo
spots.bio: Zoo in South Perth, open since 1898, with native and exotic animals and guided tours.
spots.note: South Perth, 2.5 km from the centre.

spots.name: Western Australian Maritime Museum
spots.bio: Museum on Fremantle's Victoria Quay with the America's Cup yacht Australia II and tours of the submarine HMAS Ovens.
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth. HMAS Ovens (rejected as part of this museum) goes in its bio.

spots.name: Fremantle Markets
spots.bio: Heritage market hall in Fremantle with over 150 stalls, trading Friday to Sunday.
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth. A permanent market hall trading three days a week (kept by the judge).

spots.name: Aquarium of Western Australia
spots.bio: The state aquarium at Hillarys Boat Harbour, with an underwater tunnel through its tanks.
spots.note: Hillarys, 17 km north of the centre; its own pin, about 300 m from Hillarys Boat Harbour's.

spots.name: Scarborough Beach
spots.bio: Popular surf beach on Perth's north coast, with a beachfront skate park and swimming.
spots.note: Sunset Coast, 13 km from the centre.

spots.name: Swan Bells
spots.bio: Bell tower at Barrack Square housing a peal of 18 bells, with an observation deck over the river and city.
spots.note: Central Perth.

spots.name: Caversham Wildlife Park
spots.bio: Wildlife park in Whiteman Park with about 200 species of native animals, kangaroo feeding and koala encounters.
spots.note: Inside Whiteman Park, 15 km north-east of the centre; its own pin, distinct from the park's.

spots.name: Optus Stadium
spots.bio: Perth's main stadium, hosting AFL football, cricket and major events, with behind-the-scenes stadium tours.
spots.note: Burswood, 3 km from the centre.

spots.name: WA Shipwrecks Museum
spots.bio: Free maritime archaeology museum in Fremantle's 1850s Commissariat building, displaying timbers of the Batavia.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) tourism=museum way 49736345 "Western Australian Museum Shipwrecks"
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth.

spots.name: Round House
spots.bio: Western Australia's oldest public building, built in 1831 on Arthur Head, now a free museum above Bathers Bay.
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth. Whalers' Tunnel (rejected as part of it) goes in its bio.

spots.name: Fremantle Arts Centre
spots.bio: Contemporary arts centre in a former asylum building in Fremantle, with galleries, a courtyard and a café.
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth.

spots.name: Heirisson Island
spots.bio: Island in the Swan River, reached from the Causeway, where a small mob of wild kangaroos roams.
spots.note: 2.2 km from the centre.

spots.name: Whiteman Park
spots.bio: Recreation reserve in Perth's north with bushland, museums and kangaroos, and home to Caversham Wildlife Park.
spots.note: 15 km north-east of the centre.

spots.name: Adventure World
spots.bio: Western Australia's main theme park, at Bibra Lake, with rides and waterslides; open September to April.
spots.note: Bibra Lake, 16 km south of the centre.

spots.name: Guildford
spots.bio: One of Western Australia's oldest settlements, a heritage town on the Swan River at the gateway to the Swan Valley.
spots.note: Wikivoyage Swan Valley district; 11 km north-east of the centre.

spots.name: Lake Monger
spots.bio: Inner-city lake known for its black swans, with boardwalks and a 3.5 km circuit facing the city skyline.
spots.note: 4 km north-west of the centre.

spots.name: Hillarys Boat Harbour
spots.bio: Marina on Perth's north coast with a boardwalk, a sheltered swimming beach and the state aquarium next door.
spots.note: 17 km north of the centre; its own pin, separate from the aquarium's.

spots.name: Carnac Island
spots.bio: Island nature reserve off Fremantle where Australian sea lions haul out, reached by boat for swimming and snorkelling.
spots.note: Reached by boat from Fremantle; 26 km from Perth's centre, inside the span. Not a Rockingham spot: 18 km north of it and not reached from there.

spots.name: Bathers Beach
spots.bio: Sheltered beach below Fremantle's Round House, with a licensed area on the sand and an art precinct.
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth.

spots.name: Fishing Boat Harbour
spots.bio: Fremantle's working fishing harbour, with boardwalks, fish and chips and the Bon Scott statue.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) leisure=marina way 47117508 "Fishing Boat Harbour" (centroid in the water: re-pin on the boardwalk)
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth. Named "Fishing Boat Harbour" per the judge ("Fisherman's Wharf" is only one restaurant's seating there).

spots.name: Mettam's Pool
spots.bio: Sheltered reef lagoon in Marmion Marine Park on Perth's north coast, for snorkelling close to shore.
spots.note: Sunset Coast, 14 km north-west of the centre.

spots.name: City Beach
spots.bio: Patrolled swimming beach sheltered by groynes on Perth's coast, west of the city centre.
spots.note: Sunset Coast, 9 km west of the centre.

spots.name: Trigg Beach
spots.bio: Beach beside Trigg Point on Perth's north coast, known for the city's most consistent surf break.
spots.note: Sunset Coast; one spot with Trigg Point per the judge.

spots.name: Scitech
spots.bio: Hands-on science discovery centre in West Perth with interactive galleries and a planetarium.
spots.note: West Perth, 1.8 km from the centre.

spots.name: Old Mill
spots.bio: The 1835 windmill at Mill Point by the Narrows Bridge, the oldest surviving colonial structure in the Perth area.
spots.note: South Perth, 1.9 km from the centre.

spots.name: Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts
spots.bio: Contemporary arts centre in Perth's Cultural Centre with free, changing exhibitions of local and international artists.
spots.note: Central Perth; its own pin beside the Art Gallery (the two are about 70 m apart: check pin-shared).

spots.name: Aviation Heritage Museum
spots.bio: Aviation museum at Bull Creek with about 30 civil and military aircraft, including an Avro Lancaster.
spots.note: Bull Creek, 11 km south of the centre.

spots.name: St Mary's Cathedral
spots.bio: Catholic cathedral in central Perth where the 1865 nave meets a modern curved extension and second spire.
spots.note: Central Perth.

spots.name: Kangaroos in the City
spots.bio: Larger-than-life bronze kangaroo statues on the corner of Barrack Street and St Georges Terrace in central Perth.
spots.coordinates_source: wikivoyage listing geo tag (Perth City page)
spots.note: Central Perth.

spots.name: Bold Park
spots.bio: Coastal bushland park in Perth's west with the Zamia Trail and the boardwalk up Reabold Hill to a lookout.
spots.note: 7 km west of the centre.

spots.name: Wireless Hill Park
spots.bio: Bushland park with spring wildflowers, a hilltop lookout over the Swan River and a museum in the old radio station.
spots.note: Ardross, 11 km south-west of the centre.

spots.name: Leighton Beach
spots.bio: White-sand beach at North Fremantle for swimming, surfing and kitesurfing.
spots.note: North Fremantle, filed under Perth.

spots.name: Sorrento Beach
spots.bio: Beach on Perth's north coast with a netted swimming enclosure, a reef and a picnic area.
spots.note: Beside Hillarys, 17 km north of the centre.

spots.name: South Beach
spots.bio: Family swimming beach in South Fremantle with barbecues, shade and a traditional sauna.
spots.note: South Fremantle, filed under Perth.

spots.name: Swanbourne Beach
spots.bio: Perth's only clothing-optional beach, 500 m north of the main Swanbourne swimming beach.
spots.note: 9 km west of the centre.

spots.name: Army Museum of Western Australia
spots.bio: Military museum in Fremantle's old Artillery Barracks at the foot of Cantonment Hill.
spots.note: Fremantle, filed under Perth. Cantonment Hill (review) would go in its bio.

spots.name: Perth's Outback Splash
spots.bio: Outdoor water park in the Swan Valley with nine slides, mazes and mini golf; open September to April.
spots.note: Upper Swan, 34.8 km from the centre: inside the 37.5 km reach.

spots.name: The Basin
spots.bio: Sheltered swimming beach on Rottnest Island with a shallow reef pool, patrolled in summer.
spots.note: Rottnest's best-known swimming beach, 2.7 km from the island centre.

spots.name: Wadjemup Lighthouse
spots.bio: Lighthouse on Rottnest Island's highest point, with views across the island and tours of the tower.
spots.note: Island centre, 1.6 km.

spots.name: Cathedral Rocks
spots.bio: Viewing platform at Rottnest's West End over a colony of New Zealand fur seals.
spots.note: West End of the island, about 7 km from the centre.

spots.name: Oliver Hill Battery
spots.bio: Restored WWII gun battery on Rottnest Island, with 9.2-inch guns and tunnels shown on guided tours.
spots.coordinates_source: osm:node/6420216274 (place=locality "Oliver Hill") — the hill, not the battery: re-pin on the gun emplacement
spots.note: Island centre, 0.4 km; reached by the island's heritage train.

spots.name: John Forrest National Park
spots.bio: Darling Range national park east of Perth, with walks to Rocky Pool and National Park Falls and picnic areas.
spots.note: A thin park (no separate kept spots), so a spot of the named region rather than its own destination.

spots.name: Mundaring Weir
spots.bio: Dam on the Helena River in the Perth Hills, with a walk over the weir wall, picnic areas and a museum.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) waterway=dam way 30594590 "Mundaring Weir" (Wikivoyage listing point -31.95382, 116.16522 is 330 m north)
spots.note: Lake C. Y. O'Connor, the reservoir behind it, is the same place (one spot).

spots.name: Lesmurdie Falls
spots.bio: Waterfall on the Darling Scarp in Lesmurdie Falls National Park, flowing after winter rain, with views to Perth.
spots.note: Kalamunda hills.

spots.name: Serpentine Falls
spots.bio: The main attraction of Serpentine National Park, a waterfall with a picnic ground that flows mainly in autumn and winter.
spots.note: Serpentine-Jarrahdale, part of the Perth Hills on Destination Perth's Perth Hills page.

spots.name: Lake Leschenaultia
spots.bio: Lake in the Perth Hills for swimming, canoeing and picnics, with mountain bike trails around it.
spots.note: Chidlow, the north-eastern edge of the hills.

spots.name: Kalamunda
spots.bio: Hills town at the northern end of the Bibbulmun Track, with the Kalamunda History Village and a heritage walk.
spots.note: A town with draws of its own (the History Village, the Zig Zag Cultural Centre, the Bibbulmun terminus) that no other spot covers.

spots.name: Zig Zag Scenic Drive
spots.bio: One-way scenic drive down a former railway zig-zag on the Darling Scarp, with views over Perth; also walkable.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) highway=unclassified way 1064751411 "Zig Zag Scenic Drive" (a point on the way; take the route midpoint with resolve-pin)
spots.note: Gooseberry Hill, Kalamunda hills.

spots.name: Railway Reserves Heritage Trail
spots.bio: Walking and cycling loop along the Perth Hills' former railway lines, with a trailhead at Mundaring's sculpture park.
spots.note: Named the board's spelling ("Railway Reserves") per the judge.

spots.name: Araluen Botanic Park
spots.bio: Botanic park of 59 ha in the hills near Roleystone, with camellia and heritage rose collections.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) leisure=park way 30594672 "Araluen Botanic Park" (centroid: re-pin at the entrance)
spots.note: Armadale hills (Roleystone).

spots.name: Mount Dale
spots.bio: Lookout in Helena National Park with views over the Darling Range, and a drop-off point on the Bibbulmun Track.
spots.note: Helena National Park's road-access lookout (Helena NP itself is in review as a near-duplicate of this).

spots.name: Serpentine National Park
spots.bio: Darling Range park south of Perth with the Kitty's Gorge and Baldwin's Bluff walks and spring wildflowers.
spots.note: A thin park (two kept places), so a spot of the named region.

spots.name: Walyunga National Park
spots.bio: Avon River gorge in the Darling Range with granite boulders, picnic areas, canoeing and an Aboriginal heritage trail.
spots.note: Swan hills, 30 km north-east of Perth; Wikivoyage: "covers 1,800 hectares of the Darling Range, tucked behind the Darling Scarp". Not an Avon Valley spot: it is reached from Perth by the Great Northern Highway (32 km from Perth's centre), and lies at the far western edge of the Avon Valley's circle (47 km) while the Avon Valley's visitors base in York, Northam and Toodyay.

spots.name: Cohunu Koala Park
spots.bio: Family-run wildlife sanctuary at Byford, open since 1972, with koalas, wombats, dingoes and a walk-through aviary.
spots.note: Byford, Serpentine-Jarrahdale.

spots.name: Mundaring Community Sculpture Park
spots.bio: Town park in Mundaring with works by eight Western Australian artists, including the Moodae-ring acoustic sculpture.
spots.note: Named per the judge. Mundaring (the town) is folded into it and the destination description.

spots.name: Armadale Reptile Centre
spots.bio: Wildlife centre in Armadale with more than 50 reptile species, plus kangaroos and dingoes.
spots.note: Named by Experience Perth Hills; Armadale hills.

spots.name: Penguin Island
spots.bio: Island off Rockingham with a colony of little penguins and walking trails, reached by ferry from Mersey Point.
spots.note: Rockingham's headline: the island is the spot, not the ferry.

spots.name: Point Peron
spots.bio: Headland near Rockingham with beaches, snorkelling, scenic trails, a lookout and WWII ruins.
spots.note: The hub of Rockingham Lakes Regional Park (DBCA), 6 km west of Rockingham.

spots.name: Rockingham Beach
spots.bio: Sheltered family beach on Rockingham's foreshore, the only north-facing beach in the Perth region.
spots.note: Rockingham's foreshore.

spots.name: Lake Richmond
spots.bio: Lake in Rockingham with viewing points over a critically endangered community of living thrombolites.
spots.note: 2.5 km west of the centre; distinct from the Lake Clifton Thrombolites (a different lake, 50 km south).

spots.name: Rockingham Museum
spots.bio: Local history museum in Rockingham's Art Deco former Road Board building, with interactive displays.
spots.note: Rockingham.

spots.name: Giants of Mandurah
spots.bio: Five giant recycled-wood sculptures by artist Thomas Dambo, hidden around the Mandurah area.
spots.note: Mandurah's headline draw.

spots.name: Lake Clifton Thrombolites
spots.bio: Boardwalk over thrombolites, rare living rock-like structures, on the shore of Lake Clifton in Yalgorup National Park.
spots.note: 24 km south of Mandurah, reached from it.

spots.name: Pinjarra
spots.bio: Historic Peel town on the Murray River, with a heritage trail past 19 historic sites from the Edenvale precinct.
spots.note: 18 km south-east of Mandurah.

spots.name: Dwellingup
spots.bio: Darling Range forest town and base for Lane Poole Reserve, the Bibbulmun and Munda Biddi trails and Hotham Valley Railway.
spots.note: 38.3 km from Mandurah, inside the 39 km reach; the Peel's forest town (Hotham Valley Railway, rejected as a vehicle, runs to it from Pinjarra).

spots.name: Yalgorup National Park
spots.bio: Coastal park south of Mandurah with ten Ramsar-listed lakes, tuart woodland and the Heathlands Walk Trail.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) tourism=camp_site way 1124908016 "Martins Tank" (the park's campground; a different point from the thrombolites, as the judge asked)
spots.note: A thin park (two kept places), so a spot of Mandurah; 35.5 km south.

spots.name: York
spots.bio: Historic Avon Valley town 97 km east of Perth, with one of Western Australia's best-preserved Victorian town centres.
spots.note: A town whose streetscape is the draw (Avon Terrace, in review, is part of it); its museums and lookout are separate spots.

spots.name: Toodyay
spots.bio: Historic Avon River town of 19th-century buildings, with a heritage walk and the Bilya Walk Track.
spots.note: Kept as a town with draws no other spot covers (its heritage walk and the Bilya Walk Track; Wikivoyage Perth names it a day-trip destination in itself), beside Connor's Mill and Newcastle Gaol.

spots.name: Avon Valley National Park
spots.bio: Granite outcrops and river valleys along the Avon River, with campgrounds and bushwalks.
spots.note: Reached from Toodyay; a thin park, so a spot of the region.

spots.name: Bernard Park
spots.bio: Riverside park in Northam with one of Australia's longest pedestrian suspension bridges and white swans.
spots.note: Northam's draw; Northam itself is folded into it and the destination description (town wrapper rule).

spots.name: Connor's Mill
spots.bio: Three-storey 1875 flour mill in Toodyay, still in working order and now a museum.
spots.note: Toodyay.

spots.name: Newcastle Gaol Museum
spots.bio: Toodyay's 1865 gaol, now a museum, where the legend of the bushranger Moondyne Joe began.
spots.note: Toodyay.

spots.name: York Motor Museum
spots.bio: Community-run motor museum in York with about 90 vintage cars and motorcycles.
spots.note: York.

spots.name: Mount Brown Lookout
spots.bio: Hilltop lookout above York with a 360-degree view of the town and a free picnic area.
spots.coordinates_source: OSM (Photon) tourism=viewpoint node 537502787 "Mt Brown Lookout" (peak node 3020140860 is 80 m away)
spots.note: York.

spots.name: Residency Museum
spots.bio: Local history museum in York, in the 1850s residence built for the convict depot's deputy superintendent.
spots.note: York.

spots.name: Beverley
spots.bio: One of Western Australia's first towns, in the Avon Valley south of York, with colonial architecture.
spots.note: Destination Perth gives it its own section of the Avon Valley page.

spots.name: Yanchep National Park
spots.bio: Park north of Perth with a koala boardwalk, kangaroos, guided cave tours, walking trails and a lagoon.
spots.note: 46 km north of Perth's centre, outside Perth's 37.5 km reach; a thin park (two kept places: it and Crystal Cave; Yonderup Cave in review), so standalone.

spots.name: Crystal Cave
spots.bio: Show cave in Yanchep National Park, visited only on a ticketed guided tour.
spots.note: Inside Yanchep National Park, which is standalone; named "Crystal Cave" as DBCA names it (judge).

spots.name: New Norcia
spots.bio: Australia's only monastic town, a Benedictine community with a 19th-century abbey, museum, art gallery and town tours.
spots.note: 130 km north of Perth with no destination near it.

spots.name: Gingin
spots.bio: Historic town around Gingin Brook north of Perth, with Granville Park, walking trails and heritage buildings.
spots.note: 68 km north of Perth, 31 km from Yanchep; no destination near it.

spots.name: Mount Cooke
spots.bio: The highest point of the Darling Range at 582 m, an 11 km return summit walk from the Sullivan Rock car park.
spots.note: In Monadnocks Conservation Park off Albany Highway, 45.5 km from the Perth Hills centre (outside its 40.5 km reach), 57 km from Mandurah and 56 km from Rockingham; reached on its own, so standalone. A named day section of the Bibbulmun Track, which is placed in wa-south-west.
